MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron has no clean semantic trigger: it fires weakly on short function/filler words that terminate or pivot a clause (e.g. "not", "or", "with", "go (away)", "help"), and is strongly suppressed on prepositions/articles that introduce a following noun phrase ("a", "of", "from", "out by") — i.e. it appears to encode a syntactic continuation/phrase-boundary distinction on grammatical tokens rather than any topic.

This neuron fires on tokens sitting *inside* a formal, formulaic multi-part name or set phrase — e.g., the comma separating elements of an official organization title or postal address ("Department for Culture, Media and Sport"; "Executive Drive, PO Box 123"), the "the" in "become the first…", the year-token in "2016 to 2019", "Center" in "Solar Center of Excellence" — i.e. positions where the rest of an institutional/boilerplate phrase is strongly predictable; it is suppressed at commas/prepositions in ordinary descriptive noun phrases ("a small, vocal group", "members of the group").
